item.title: Assembly Drill 2026-11-23: crackme
item.description:
# Crackme: find the number (Windows x64, arg in ecx)
`ecx` holds an unsigned 32-bit number.
``` check: mov eax, ecx ; eax = copy of x shr eax, 1 ; eax = x >> 1 (shift right, top bit filled with 0) xor eax, ecx ; eax = (x >> 1) ^ x cmp eax, 0Fh jne fail mov eax, 1 ret fail: xor eax, eax ret ```
What value of `x` makes `check` return 1?
Hint: this one is not a simple "undo each step backwards". The xor mixes `x` with a shifted copy of *itself*, so work in binary, one bit at a time, starting from the top.
---
**Answer:** `x = 10` (0b1010)
1. Each result bit is `x[i] ^ x[i+1]`, i.e. the bit XORed with its left-hand neighbour. The top bit has a 0 to its left (shr fills with 0), so it passes through unchanged. 2. Target 0b1111: every bit above bit 3 is 0, so x has nothing above bit 3, and bit 3 = 1. Moving down, each next bit = the result bit XOR the x bit just above it: 1^1=0, 1^0=1, 1^1=0, giving 1010. 3. Check: 1010 ^ 0101 = 1111 = 0Fh. (`x ^ (x >> 1)` is the "Gray code" of x, and the answer is unique.)
